key_insight: SpecGP is a transformer-based model that predicts collision-energy–adaptable structural MS/MS spectra for N‑glycopeptides, enhancing fragment ion coverage to discriminate isomers and improve identification confidence via rescoring.
problem_solved: Collision-energy-dependent fragmentation of glycopeptides is complex and poorly modeled, limiting accurate isomer identification and confidence in glycoproteomics results.
method: Transformer model conditioned on peptide/glycan sequence and collision energy to predict fragment ion intensities across energies.
Design focused on enhancing structural fragment ion coverage (not just peptide backbone ions) to capture glycan-specific fragmentation patterns.
Integration of predicted spectra into rescoring pipelines to improve peptide-spectrum matches and isomer discrimination.
impact: Enables energy-aware spectral prediction that improves identification accuracy and structural interpretation in glycoproteomics; AI/ML practitioners can adopt energy-conditioned models to boost domain-specific identification tasks.

paper_title: SpecGP as a transformer-based model for predicting energy-adaptable structural spectra of glycopeptides
paper_authors: Xianyong Wang, Rui Song, Zhuangzhuang Feng, Shisheng Sun
